Nesting Comments Under a Ticket

A Comment never has its own top-level URL — it's only ever reached through the ticket it belongs to.

Comment isn't a standalone resource the way Ticket and Tag are — the domain model says a comment always belongs to exactly one ticket, and the URLs follow that: /tickets/1/comments, not /comments. Getting there is two routers, not one — comment.routes.js, mounted inside ticket.routes.js:

// Figure 3.11: mounting a nested router (src/routes/comment.routes.js, and the mount point in src/routes/ticket.routes.js)
// comment.routes.js
const router = express.Router({ mergeParams: true });
router.get('/', validate({ params: ticketIdParamSchema }), commentController.getAllComments);
// ...post/:id routes follow the same shape

// ticket.routes.js
router.use('/:ticketId/comments', commentRoutes);

router.use('/:ticketId/comments', commentRoutes) means every request under that path — GET /tickets/1/comments, DELETE /tickets/1/comments/9, all of it — gets handed off to comment.routes.js to actually match. The :ticketId part is already consumed by ticket.routes.js by the time that handoff happens, though — which is exactly the problem { mergeParams: true } solves. Without it, a nested router only ever sees params matched within its own path (an :id from /:id inside comment.routes.js itself, say) — req.params.ticketId would be undefined in every comment controller, because as far as that inner router is concerned, :ticketId belongs to a different router entirely. { mergeParams: true } tells Express to merge the parent router's matched params into req.params too, so commentController. getAllComments can read req.params.ticketId like any other param.
